mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in the past three months signals an improving labor market, which typically boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of decreasing unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP by more than 2% in the past six months signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong GDP growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in the past month signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of decreasing industrial production compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 in the past month signals a strong labor market, which typically boosts consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong payroll growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a strong demand side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of joint increases in housing starts and personal consumption compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate coupled with an increase in the consumer price index signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decrease & CPIAUCSL increase in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of decreasing federal funds rate and increasing CPI compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decrease & PAYEMS increase in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of decreasing unemployment and increasing payrolls compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
